summary.headline: Manorama FY26 standalone revenue rose 76.1% to INR 1,357 crore with EBITDA margin of 27.1% and PAT of INR 233.2 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 standalone revenue grew 76.1% YoY to about INR 1,357 crore, with EBITDA of INR 367.7 crore (27.1% margin) and PAT of INR 233.2 crore (17.2% margin). Q4 standalone revenue was INR 382.3 crore, EBITDA INR 102.9 crore (26.9%) and PAT INR 59.5 crore (15.6%), with a forex net loss of INR 7.58 crore after a INR 17.05 crore mark-to-market provision. Management announced a roughly INR 460 crore capex plan over two to three years covering solvent fractionation, a cocoa butter alternatives plant, refining and Burkina Faso raw material processing. Consolidated margins were softer as nine new subsidiaries were in their first year, and the company filed revised results due to a wrong file being uploaded.

financial_highlights.change: Margin expansion of about 230 bps per analyst question, confirmed as mix and efficiency driven

financial_highlights.value: INR 7.58 crore (MTM provision INR 17.05 crore, forex income INR 9.47 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Cumulative FY26 MTM provision INR 23.3 crore

financial_highlights.value: approx INR 710 crore (raw material ~INR 420 crore, finished goods ~INR 260 crore, co-products and WIP ~INR 30 crore)

segments.name: Solvent fractionation
segments.commentary: Plant 2 capacity raised 30% from 25,000 to 32,500 tpa via debottlenecking; plant 1 (15,000 t) debottlenecking planned this fiscal. Total fractionation capacity stated at 47,500 t, expected to reach 52,000 t.

segments.name: Cocoa butter equivalent (CBE)
segments.commentary: CBE contributed about 30% of revenue versus about 10% two years earlier; FY26 CBE volume about 7,500 t. Stearin volume about 8,000 t in FY26; stearin plus CBE together about 70-75% of revenue.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (nine, mostly first year)
segments.commentary: Seven audited African subsidiaries posted about INR 13.5 crore losses in FY26, about INR 6 crore in Q4. Consolidated EBITDA margin about 26% versus 27% standalone; management called start-up costs one-time.

segments.name: Dekel (Brazil, LATAM)
segments.commentary: Processing on a per-tonne cost model with no profit sharing; operations only just started, with minimal volume. One subsidiary showed about INR 9 crore revenue and INR 5 crore loss in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable margin range guided at 25-27% EBITDA and 45-50% gross margin; management said it is a yearly rather than quarterly guide.
FY27 expected to be a strong growth year, volume-led with 5-10% price realisation; management cited 30% volume growth from debottlenecking plus 5-10% pricing.
Management said utilisation of about 85-90% of the 52,000 t fractionation capacity is targeted for FY27.

Capex of about INR 460 crore over two to three years, with projects targeted for commissioning by FY28; forward integration (CBA plant, 75,000 t SF3, 90,000 t refinery) about INR 330-340 crore with asset turn above 6x.
Management reiterated long-term target of more than INR 3,500 crore revenue by FY30 and said it is confident on achieving it.
Working capital cycle and margins expected to hold for the next one to two years, with updates given quarterly if headwinds emerge.
capex_capacity: Solvent fractionation plant 2 debottlenecked from 25,000 to 32,500 tpa; overall fractionation capacity 47,500 t per company, expected to reach 52,000 t after the plant 1 debottlenecking (debottlenecking cost under INR 8-10 crore).
Burkina Faso raw material processing unit capex about INR 120 crore, aimed at saving freight and improving butter yield (butter about 45-60% of raw material).
Forward integration project (CBA plant, SF3 of 75,000 t, 90,000 t refinery) about INR 330-340 crore; about INR 52 crore spent so far (INR 16 crore WIP), and land acquired for the Indian plant.

Overall INR 460 crore programme includes a new solvent fractionation facility for Sal, Shea, Palm, Mango and other exotic seeds, a cocoa butter alternatives facility, and an additional 200 tpd refinery.
Funding through internal accruals (about INR 130 crore fixed deposits); QIP enabling approval up to INR 500 crore, with no decision yet.
demand_pricing: FY26 volume growth about 80-90% and price growth about 5-10%, per management in Q&A.
Existing capacity utilisation about 85% on 40,000 t; around 15% spare headroom on the existing plant.
Export share about 57% of revenue; around 60% of net forex exposure hedged through forwards.
Middle East exposure about 2-3% of revenue; management said direct impact of the West Asia conflict is limited, with indirect effects via energy, freight and currency.
Management said some raw material (Sal, Mango, Shea) is not sourced from affected regions.
Manorama Africa supplied about 20-25% of raw material purchases in FY26 versus about 60% previously cited by an analyst; FY27 share to follow the same procurement line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Burkina Faso processing capex, capacity and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR 120 crore; it removes freight and logistics on seed imports and lifts butter yield (butter about 45-60% of raw material). Management expects it to support sustainable margins.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and working capital sustainability with capex ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow about INR 260 crore; capex phased; management expects to maintain working capital and inventory days and the 25-27% margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25-30% growth realistic and what drives FY27/FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth expected to be volume-led (30% from debottlenecking) plus 5-10% price, with spare capacity of about 15% still to be utilised. Management did not give a precise growth range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated gross margin fall from 48% to 43%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to first-year operations of new subsidiaries, with higher freight, production and setup costs; said 45-50% gross margin is the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the results revised?
qa_highlights.answer: A wrong file was uploaded inadvertently due to a technical issue; the revision is corrective and the revised financials should be used.

qa_highlights.question: Dekel arrangement and subsidiary losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Dekel is a processing-cost model paid per tonne processed, with no profit sharing. Subsidiary losses were attributed to first-year setup costs and expected to normalise; no separate breakdown was given.

qa_highlights.question: Funding plan and QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex funded from internal accruals so far; QIP of up to INR 500 crore is an enabling approval only, with options being evaluated and disclosures to follow if finalised.

risks_watch: Consolidated margins and losses from nine subsidiaries, with Q4 African subsidiary losses of about INR 6 crore; management expects normalisation.
Gross margin compression at consolidated level (48% to 43% QoQ per analyst) and whether it reverses.
Execution of INR 460 crore capex and FY28 commissioning timelines; forward integration returns not yet disclosed in INR terms.
Forex exposure: INR 23.3 crore cumulative MTM provision in FY26 with 40% of net exposure unhedged.
Political and currency risk in Burkina Faso; management cited an MoU with the Burkina Faso government.
Revised results filing and the need for better disclosure consistency (consolidated figures not in press release; OER requested by analyst).
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity, with a steady line on margins, but guarded and repetitive when pressed on subsidiary losses, consolidated margins and the QIP. Several answers were vague on numbers, such as the 4,500 t debottlenecking timing and Dekel volumes.
key_quotes: FY 2026 has been a year of exceptional performance.
We are not expecting any downward pressure on the margin from the current level.
Around a 60% of our company's net forcign exchange is currently hedged through forward contracts.
CBE has contributed around 30% to our top linc.
